1. Rule.
Rule is made returnable forthwith.
Ms. Gauri Rao, the learned APP waives notice on behalf of the Respondent No.1 and 2-State and Shri _____Page No. 1 of 6____ 15th May 2024 Gaikwad RD 40-iast-10941-2024.docx
Dhiraj Jain, the learned counsel waives notice on behalf of the Respondent No.3.
With consent of the parties, matter is taken up for final disposal.

2. The Petitioner seeks quashing of complaint vide CR No.62 of 2023 registered with Respondent No.2 emanating from FIR No.627/2023 registered with the Chembur Police Station, for offenses punishable under Sections 120-B, 420, 465, 467, 471, 468 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC").
3. The Petitioner was the Chairman and Managing Director of MEP Infrastructure Developers Ltd. (MEP IDL), a company engaged in construction, operation and maintenance of road infrastructure in India.

The gist of allegations made against him by Respondent No.3-Complainant are that he allegedly colluded with the employees of Janakalyan Sahkari Bank Ltd. ( JKSBL) and entered into a criminal conspiracy and forged documents relating to a resolution passed by the Board of Yashyog Infrastructure and Development Pvt. Ltd. (YIDPL), a company of Respondent No.3 and bill discounting facility, submitting the same as genuine with JKSBL for availing bill discounting facility worth Rs.9,45,30,420/- and thus committed the offenses alleged in the FIR.

entities.text: Yashyog Infrastructure and Development Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Recovery proceedings were filed by JKSBL before the Deputy Registrar, Mumbai for recovery of the outstanding loan against the Respondent No.3-Complainant in respect of the bill discounting _____Page No. 2 of 6____ 15th May 2024 Gaikwad RD 40-iast-10941-2024.docx facility availed by YIDPL.
The Petitioner states that this led to a misunderstanding between him and the Respondent No.3 prompting him to lodge the said FIR.
The investigation was initiated.

On the basis of the said FIR and the investigation that followed, a Look Out Circular (LOC) was issued against the Petitioner causing the inconvenience and loss of reputation to the Petitioner.
4.
It appears that in the interregnum, the parties decided to amicably resolve their disputes.
The Respondent No.3 has withdrawn his complaint before the Respondent No.2 by his letter dated 3rd May 2024.
The said letter is taken on record and marked as 'X1' for identification.

The JKSBL by their letter dated 30th January 2024 granted time to MEP IDL to make payment of the principal amount of Rs.588 Lakhs and accordingly MEP IDL by its letter dated 31st January 2024 accepted the terms of payment of principal amount to be payable to JKSBL.

Thus, vide letter dated 3rd February 2024, MEP IDL made payment of Rs.Two Crores to JKSBL; by letter dated 23rd February 2024, a payment of Rs.1.94 crores has been made; and, by letter dated 5th March 2024, a further payment of an amount of Rs.1.94 crores is also made by MEP IDL to JKSBL.
All the letters are placed on record as Exhibit F, G and H at pages 38, 39 and 41of the petition respectively.

sentences.text: _ _ _ __Page No. 3 of 6____ 15th May 2024 Gaikwad RD 40-iast-10941-2024.docx
Photocopies of cheques are also placed on record at pages 42 and 43 of the petition.
5. The Respondent No.3 has also filed his consent affidavit dated 10th March 2024 affirmed and duly attested before a Notary Public, Mumbai.
The same is at Page 46 of the Petition.
In the said affidavit, the Respondent No.3 has stated that the parties have sorted out their differences and the complaint was filed on account of misunderstanding between the parties.
They now wish to put an end to the acrimony and settle the dispute amicably.
The Respondent No.3 stated that he does not wish to proceed with his complaint nor continue the prosecution against the Petitioner.

5. The Consent Terms executed by and between the parties also indicate that the parties have worked out a settlement with a desire to lead their respective lives and pursue their individual business activities peacefully.
6. The parties are present in Court.
The Respondent No.3 is identified by his advocate.
On questioning, he reiterates his stand in the Consent Terms and the affidavit.

He further states that in view of the settlement, he has no objection to quashing of CR No. 62 of 2023 registered with the Respondent No.2 emanating from FIR No.627/2023 registered with the Chembur Police Station for offences punishable under Sections 120-B, 420, 465, 467, 471 & 468 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 _____Page No. 4 of 6____ 15th May 2024 Gaikwad RD 40-iast-10941-2024.docx 7.
Considering the nature of the dispute, relations between the parties, Consent Terms filed by the parties and the affidavit of the Respondent No.3 there is no impediment in allowing the Petition.
8. The Petitioner is, accordingly, allowed.

CR No. 62 of 2023 registered with the Respondent No.2 emanating from FIR No.627/2023 registered with the Chembur Police Station for offences punishable under Sections 120-B, 420, 465, 467, 471 & 468 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 is quashed and set aside.
In view of quashing of the said FIR, the LOC issued by the authorities in pursuance of the said FIR also stands quashed.
It is made clear that it is only the LOC issued and relatable to CR No.62/2023 emanating from FIR NO.627/2023, i.e., the subject matter of the present proceedings which stands quashed and set aside.
We have not dealt with any other LOC relatable to any other case, if pending against the Petitioner.

The Petitioner is directed to deposit an amount of Rs. 2,00,000/- towards costs in the Central Police Welfare Fund in Saving Account No.914010029005759 in the Axis Bank, Worli, Mumbai having IFSC No. UTIB0000060, within a period of 3 weeks from the uploading of this order.
The Petitioner is directed to file a compliance affidavit along with the proof of deposit of costs within a week thereafter, failing which the petition will stand revived.
9. Rule is made absolute in the aforesaid terms.
